workstream: W0-5 (alert plane runs without a human)
purpose: Viewer-only service account for the alert-plane drift verification lanes: `ops-plane-verify.yml` job `alert-plane-drift` and `ops-confidence.yml` job `deploy-freshness`. It reads live GCP alert policies, billing budgets, log sinks, and IAM posture and compares them against the committed source of truth. It can never mutate production: every role below is a viewer role.

roleConstraints.rationale: The lanes this identity serves are drift DETECTORS. A writer role here would let a CI compromise mutate the alert plane it is supposed to guard (and would contradict the fail-closed drift contract: the file wins, live is the bug). cloudfunctions.viewer and run.viewer exist only so deploy-freshness can list Cloud Functions and get Cloud Run services (scripts/ci/check-deploy-freshness.mjs); both are read-only.

workloadIdentityFederation.assertion: The Google Cloud identity is minted only for OIDC tokens from scheduled or dispatched runs of ops-plane-verify.yml and ops-confidence.yml on refs/heads/main of Imagine-That-Ai/BurnBar: the provider's attribute condition pins repository, ref, and job_workflow_ref, so a same-repository PR branch (or any other workflow) cannot impersonate ops-verifier even though the service-account binding is the repository principal set (same pattern as docs/ops/STAGING.md).

gcloud: gcloud iam service-accounts create ops-verifier --project=burnbar --display-name='Ops plane verifier (viewer-only)'

for ROLE in roles/monitoring.viewer roles/billing.viewer roles/logging.viewer roles/iam.securityReviewer roles/cloudfunctions.viewer roles/run.viewer; do gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding burnbar --member='serviceAccount:ops-verifier@burnbar.iam.gserviceaccount.com' --role="$ROLE"; done

gcloud iam workload-identity-pools describe github-oidc --project=burnbar --location=global >/dev/null 2>&1 || gcloud iam workload-identity-pools create github-oidc --project=burnbar --location=global --display-name='GitHub OIDC'

gcloud iam workload-identity-pools providers create-oidc github-oidc --project=burnbar --location=global --workload-identity-pool=github-oidc --issuer-uri='https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com' --attribute-mapping='google.subject=assertion.sub,attribute.repository=assertion.repository,attribute.ref=assertion.ref,attribute.job_workflow_ref=assertion.job_workflow_ref' --attribute-condition="assertion.repository=='Imagine-That-Ai/BurnBar' && assertion.ref=='refs/heads/main' && (assertion.job_workflow_ref=='Imagine-That-Ai/BurnBar/.github/workflows/ops-plane-verify.yml@refs/heads/main' || assertion.job_workflow_ref=='Imagine-That-Ai/BurnBar/.github/workflows/ops-confidence.yml@refs/heads/main')"
githubRepoVariables: gh variable set OPS_BILLING_ACCOUNT --body '<billing-account-id>'   # lets alert-plane-drift compare the live budget with governance/ops-billing-budget.json

behaviorUntilProvisioned.detail: Both jobs exit 1 with `::error::wif-not-provisioned` on schedule/dispatch while the two repo variables are absent. This is the honest signal the wave-0 verdict requires: the alert plane flips from silent `waiting` to a loud, named red. The check scripts themselves are still gated on every PR via the `drift-check-selftest` job, so drift-detection capability never regresses while the identity is provisioned.

notGoals: The GCP_SA_KEY protected lane (`verify` job) is unchanged — it keeps `environment: production` + `credentials_json` and is asserted by scripts/ci/verify-ops-plane-workflow-boundary.mjs (invariant SWAP, not deletion).
No deploy/age_days custom metric: that would need roles/monitoring.metricWriter, a write role this identity must never hold (human queue item 8).
No budget-notification Cloud Function: applying the budget stays a human-run script (scripts/ops/create-billing-budget.sh --dry-run first).

budgetDrift.detail: The alert-plane-drift lane reads the live budget (gcloud billing budgets list, roles/billing.viewer) and fails closed on a missing budget, a changed amount, thresholds, project filter, or notification topic, and on a missing OPS_BILLING_ACCOUNT variable (billing-account-not-configured).
